title: A poster on how textures wear, and a second place

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine a virtual leather boot that scuffs a little more with every step you take, in real time. That was the idea on Antoine's poster at CAÉC 2026.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The annual congress of student researchers. Antoine presented a poster on simulating the visual wear of textures in real time, driven by experimental data, so the wear is grounded in measurements rather than guesswork.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He placed second in the Optics category.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. What did people talk about at the poster?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A nice spread: automatic commit classification, training models with other models, and optics. He also chatted with Samuel Lefebvre about virtual reality interaction and what makes a virtual world feel more believable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So wear is part of making a virtual world believable.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the link. Surfaces that age convincingly make a scene feel lived in. The closing ceremony was hosted by Leyla Agosti Cagalli Burri, and the LinkedIn post links a paper related to work shown at the congress.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where can people read more about the wear work itself?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In Antoine's thesis write-up, the article on wear in texture space. The page links to it, so the full story is one click away.
